confidence_notes: Restaurant and drink anchors come from aggregated but crowd-sourced or secondary sources with small samples (Cities Insider, Expatistan, and a French price site), so they are rough. Cappuccino ($6-7), cocktail ($14-22) and pint ($7-12) ranges cluster consistently across sources. Inexpensive and mid-range meal anchors rely on a casual-lunch range ($16-22) and a mid-range dinner range ($30-55 per person). No direct current source for wine-by-the-glass was found, so wine_glass is a bounded estimate set relative to the beer anchor, not a sourced price. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge and city context; no accommodation searches or live listings were checked. The FX value is the most recent RBA page observation I could verify (20 March 2026), which is likely not the latest observation as of 2026-11-19.
comparable_city_reasoning: No comparable city was needed. Seattle is a US city, so the anchors use US major-city price levels. Food and drink anchors are informed by Seattle-specific aggregated sources, which report prices above the US national average. Accommodation is a general-knowledge estimate for a mid-sized US West Coast metro with strong tourism demand.
